summary: Doctor is the loop's preflight environment checker: it runs 30+ async DoctorChecks across categories (Core, Platform, Languages, Rust/Python/Node/Go tools, ComputerControl, Container, Browser, Security, Configuration), verifies the Rust MSRV, inspects selfware log health, and validates the loaded Config. Each DoctorCheck carries an Ok/Warning/Missing status, optional version, and an actionable fix_hint; the DoctorReport rolls these into OverallHealth (Healthy/Degraded/Broken) and an exit code. It gates whether the loop even has the tools it needs before the first act.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/doctor.rs read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where doctor runs before the loop starts to confirm required tools and a valid Config exist, exiting non-zero if any required check FAILs.

examples.title: Preflight the environment before the loop starts
examples.intent: Confirm all required tools exist before spending budget on the first act.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The DoctorReport gates loop entry: a Broken health with a required Missing check exits non-zero, so the loop never begins against a broken environment.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the doctor node runs a full preflight and stamps the loop's start gate.
touch_interaction.visual: A health badge fills: green Healthy, amber Degraded, red Broken; the start gate unlocks only when not Broken.

examples.mini_scenario: Doctor finds git and rustc present but ripgrep Missing; health is Degraded so the loop starts with a warning.
examples.pitfall: Only required (Core) failures should block; treating an optional Missing as fatal needlessly refuses to start.

examples.title: Check a single tool with a timeout
examples.intent: Verify one binary is present and get its version without hanging.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: check_tool runs the version command under CHECK_TIMEOUT (5s) and yields a DoctorCheck, so a stuck binary degrades gracefully instead of freezing preflight.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a tool chip re-probes just that tool.
touch_interaction.visual: The chip spins briefly; resolves to green with a version string or red 'Missing'.

examples.mini_scenario: check_tool('rg') returns Ok with 'ripgrep 14.1.0'; a hung binary would time out to Missing after 5s.
examples.pitfall: Some tools print version to stderr; a check that only reads stdout wrongly reports a present tool as Missing.

examples.title: Run all checks concurrently
examples.intent: Keep preflight fast by probing every tool in parallel.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Heterogeneous CheckFut futures are collected and driven with join_all, so 30+ checks complete in roughly the slowest single probe rather than their sum.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the doctor node fans out all check chips at once, each resolving independently.
touch_interaction.visual: Dozens of chips light up simultaneously and flip to their status as each future resolves.

examples.mini_scenario: All 30 checks fan out; the whole preflight finishes in ~5s bounded by the slowest timeout, not 150s.
examples.pitfall: Each check must be independent; a check that mutates shared state under join_all can race the others.

examples.title: Verify the project MSRV
examples.intent: Ensure the installed Rust toolchain meets the minimum supported version.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: check_msrv compares the toolchain against MSRV ('1.91'); a too-old toolchain yields a Missing/Warning DoctorCheck that flags a build risk before the loop compiles anything.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the Rust chip shows detected version vs required MSRV side by side.
touch_interaction.visual: A version dial reads green if >= 1.91, amber if below with the gap highlighted.

examples.mini_scenario: Detected rustc 1.89 vs MSRV 1.91 raises a Warning, warning the loop that compilation may fail.
examples.pitfall: MSRV is kept in sync with Cargo.toml's rust-version; a drifted constant misreports the true floor.

examples.title: Validate the loaded Config
examples.intent: Catch a broken endpoint or bad paths before the loop uses them.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: config_checks parses the endpoint URL, resolves allowed_paths glob roots, and checks for an api_key on remote endpoints, so a misconfigured loop is caught at foundation, not mid-run.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the config chip runs the pure config sanity checks.
touch_interaction.visual: Each config aspect (endpoint, paths, key) gets its own sub-chip; a bad endpoint flashes red.

examples.mini_scenario: config_checks flags 'invalid endpoint `htp://x`' as Missing so the loop doesn't fail on its first API call.
examples.pitfall: config_checks is pure (no LLM I/O); a passing config here still doesn't prove the endpoint is actually reachable.

examples.title: Warn on the cwd-shadows-global config trap
examples.intent: Explain why a global config seems ignored.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: config_checks detects when a cwd selfware.toml shadows ~/.config/selfware/config.toml and surfaces it as a DoctorCheck message, so the loop's operator understands which config is actually in effect.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the config-file chip shows the full precedence chain.
touch_interaction.visual: The active config path glows; a shadowed global is drawn ghosted beneath it with a warning tag.

examples.mini_scenario: Doctor reports 'config: ./selfware.toml (shadowing ~/.config/selfware/config.toml)' clearing up the confusion.
examples.pitfall: This is Ok-status informational; treating a legitimate cwd override as an error would be a false alarm.

examples.title: Inspect selfware log health
examples.intent: Surface recent errors and anomalies from the engine's own logs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: check_log_health scans the newest log file (500 lines) for error lines and anomalies, turning the loop's own past into a Warning DoctorCheck with a `tail` fix_hint.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the log-health chip scrolls the recent error summary.
touch_interaction.visual: A green chip when clean; amber with an error/anomaly count when the last run left errors.

examples.mini_scenario: check_log_health reports '12 error lines, 3 anomalies in selfware.log.2026-07-29' with a tail hint.
examples.pitfall: It only scans the newest 500 lines; a problem older than that window won't show in the health check.

examples.title: Roll checks into OverallHealth
examples.intent: Collapse many checks into a single go/degraded/no-go verdict.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DoctorReport computes OverallHealth from the worst required status, giving the loop one Healthy/Degraded/Broken signal to branch on instead of 30 individual results.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the doctor node collapses all chips into one health verdict badge.
touch_interaction.visual: The badge takes the color of the worst required check: green, amber, or red.

examples.mini_scenario: One Missing Core tool among 29 passing yields Broken; the loop halts with a non-zero exit code.
examples.pitfall: A single required Missing dominates the verdict; don't mark optional tools required or you'll block on non-essentials.

examples.title: Categorize checks by concern
examples.intent: Let the operator scan health by area (Core, Languages, Security...).
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each DoctorCheck carries a Category, so the report groups results and the loop can decide, e.g., to proceed with BrowserAutomation missing but not Core.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading a category header expands its member checks.
touch_interaction.visual: Category headers show a rollup color; expanding reveals the per-tool chips beneath.

examples.mini_scenario: The Security category is all-green while ContainerTools shows docker Missing, an optional gap the loop tolerates.
examples.pitfall: Category is advisory for grouping; the loop's block decision must key off required-vs-optional, not category alone.

examples.title: Attach an actionable fix_hint to every failure
examples.intent: Let the operator (or agent) fix a gap without reading docs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each failing DoctorCheck carries a fix_hint (e.g. an install command), so a Degraded loop can hand the agent a concrete remediation to act on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a red chip reveals its fix_hint as a copyable command.
touch_interaction.visual: A hint card slides out beneath the failing chip with a one-line remediation.

examples.mini_scenario: ripgrep Missing shows fix_hint 'brew install ripgrep', which the agent runs then re-checks.
examples.pitfall: Hints are best-effort per platform; a macOS-only hint may be wrong on Linux, so validate before auto-running.

examples.title: Probe an npx-delivered tool
examples.intent: Verify a tool that runs via npx rather than a global binary.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: check_npx_tool probes a Node-delivered tool under the NodeTools category, so the loop knows whether npx-based tooling (e.g. an MCP server) is usable before wiring it in.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing an npx tool chip re-runs the indirect probe.
touch_interaction.visual: The chip shows a small 'npx' tag; resolves green if the package resolves, red otherwise.

examples.mini_scenario: check_npx_tool for a language server confirms it resolves, so the loop enables that LSP integration.
examples.pitfall: npx probes can hit the network on first run; a slow probe may time out even when the tool is installable.

examples.title: Check macOS accessibility permission
examples.intent: Confirm computer-control has the OS permission it needs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: check_accessibility (platform-gated) reports whether Accessibility is granted, so the loop disables the ComputerControl act path when the permission is missing rather than failing mid-gesture.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the accessibility chip re-queries the OS permission state.
touch_interaction.visual: A lock icon opens green when granted, stays red-locked when denied.

examples.mini_scenario: Accessibility is denied, so the loop keeps computer-control tools disabled and warns the operator to grant it.
examples.pitfall: This check is platform-specific; on non-macOS the check has a different implementation and shouldn't be assumed present.

examples.title: Verify screen-capture (xcap) support
examples.intent: Confirm the screenshot backend actually works on this platform.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: check_xcap probes screen capture, so the loop only enables visual-verification/computer-vision act steps when capture is functional.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the capture chip attempts a test screenshot.
touch_interaction.visual: A camera icon flashes; green with a thumbnail on success, red on failure.

examples.mini_scenario: check_xcap succeeds, so the loop enables screenshot-based verify steps for UI work.
examples.pitfall: Capture can succeed but be empty under headless/permission constraints; a green here isn't a guarantee of usable pixels.

examples.title: Run doctor as a CLI subcommand
examples.intent: Let the operator diagnose the environment on demand.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: `selfware doctor` prints the report and returns exit_code(), giving CI and operators a scriptable health gate outside the running loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the doctor node toward the terminal lane runs it as a CLI command.
touch_interaction.visual: A terminal panel prints the categorized report; the exit code chip turns green (0) or red (non-zero).

examples.mini_scenario: CI runs `selfware doctor`; a Broken health returns a non-zero exit and fails the pipeline early.
examples.pitfall: exit_code maps Broken to non-zero; CI that ignores the exit code loses the gate's protective value.

examples.title: Feed doctor results into llm_doctor
examples.intent: Reuse config sanity checks as the first step of LLM diagnostics.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: config_checks and CheckStatus are consumed by llm_doctor's Step 0, so the LLM-backend diagnosis inherits the same validated Config foundation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing an edge from the config chip to the llm_doctor node chains the checks.
touch_interaction.visual: The config sub-chips replicate into the llm_doctor node's Step 0 lane.

examples.mini_scenario: llm_doctor imports config_checks so an invalid endpoint is caught once and reused across both diagnostics.
examples.pitfall: CheckStatus maps into CheckOutcome (Ok->Pass, Warning->Warn, Missing->Fail); a mismatched mapping mislabels severity downstream.

examples.title: Warn on optional language toolchain gaps
examples.intent: Let the loop proceed with reduced capability rather than fail.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A Missing Python/Node/Go tool yields a Warning (not a required failure), so the reason stage can plan around the gap while OverallHealth stays Degraded, not Broken.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the Languages category shows which toolchains are present.
touch_interaction.visual: Present toolchains glow green; missing ones show amber 'optional' tags, not red.

examples.mini_scenario: Go is missing but the task is Rust-only; the loop runs Degraded and simply avoids Go-language verification.
examples.pitfall: Degraded is not Broken; treating every optional gap as fatal denies otherwise-runnable tasks.

examples.title: Report a tool version for compatibility
examples.intent: Record which version of a tool the loop will call.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DoctorCheck.version captures the detected version, so the observe stage can correlate later tool behavior with the exact binary version in play.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a green tool chip reveals its detected version.
touch_interaction.visual: The version string appears as a small mono-font tag under the chip.

examples.mini_scenario: Doctor records 'git 2.45.0'; a later git behavior quirk is traced back to that version.
examples.pitfall: Version is Optional; a tool present but with an unparsed version shows Ok-with-None, not a failure.

examples.title: Re-run doctor after remediation
examples.intent: Confirm a fix actually resolved a Missing check.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After the agent runs a fix_hint, re-running the relevant DoctorCheck verifies the transition from Missing to Ok before the loop trusts the tool.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a just-fixed chip re-probes it.
touch_interaction.visual: The chip animates from red through amber to green on a successful re-check.

examples.mini_scenario: After installing ripgrep, re-running the check flips it Ok and OverallHealth returns to Healthy.
examples.pitfall: Re-check the specific tool, not the whole report, or a slow full fanout wastes budget verifying one fix.

examples.title: Gate security-sensitive act steps
examples.intent: Ensure security tooling is present before risky operations.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A Missing Security-category check lets control withhold security-dependent act steps, so the loop degrades safely rather than acting without its guardrail tools.

outputs_to: control gate on risky act steps

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the Security header shows which guard tools are available.
touch_interaction.visual: A shield header glows green when the security set is complete, amber when partial.

examples.mini_scenario: A secret-scanner is Missing, so the loop refuses to auto-commit until the guard is restored.
examples.pitfall: Doctor reports presence, not correctness; a present-but-misconfigured security tool still passes here.

examples.title: Print the human-readable report
examples.intent: Give a person a scannable health readout of the environment.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DoctorReport.print renders categorized, color-coded checks with fix hints beneath failures, translating the loop's foundation state into human-actionable output.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the report node zooms from the health badge into the full printed breakdown.
touch_interaction.visual: A scrollable panel lists checks by category with green/amber/red markers and inline fix hints.

examples.mini_scenario: The printed report shows 28 Ok, 2 Warning, 0 Missing with two fix hints, and an overall Degraded verdict.
examples.pitfall: The print is presentation only; automated callers should read the structured checks/exit_code, not scrape the text.
